description:
Redwood Inference is adding a performance regression gate to its CI/release process to prevent runtime and platform changes from silently degrading latency/throughput/cost on the company’s most important hosted models and GPU SKUs. The project introduces (1) automated perf canaries that run representative inference workloads (prefill/decode mixes, varying sequence lengths, batching settings) on a fixed set of GPU types (e.g., H100/A100/L4 class) and top hosted models, (2) a baseline/threshold system that compares new results vs. a pinned reference (last-good release or rolling baseline) with statistically defensible noise handling, and (3) a release-block mechanism that fails CI and/or blocks promotion to production when regressions exceed agreed thresholds.

Goals:
- Detect and stop meaningful performance regressions before merge/release (p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, time-to-first-token, GPU memory headroom, tail latency under load).
- Standardize what “performance regression” means at Redwood (metrics, environments, warmup, sample sizes, confidence rules).
- Reduce firefighting and customer-impacting incidents tied to runtime changes, driver/kernel updates, scheduling tweaks, or build/flag changes.
- Provide fast triage signals (links to dashboards, regression diffs, candidate commits/PRs) so Runtime/Infra/SRE can act quickly.

Non-goals:
- Replacing the full offline benchmark lab; this gate targets a curated set of canary workloads and top SKUs/models.
- Guaranteeing absolute customer SLO compliance for every workload; the gate is a preventative control for the release pipeline.

Stakeholders:
- Runtime org (Mateo Alvarez, Hiro Tanaka, Sofia Ivanova, Noah Patel, Grace Kim, Omar El‑Sayed): defines workloads, integrates runtime instrumentation, owns regressions.
- Release Engineering (Connor O’Brien, Sahana Iyer): owns CI integration, policy enforcement, and release-block plumbing.
- SRE/Observability (Sean Gallagher, Rafael Mendes, Allison Grant): defines operational thresholds, alerting/dashboards, and escalation playbooks.
- Infra/Fleet (Irene Choi, Vanessa Ortiz): provides stable canary capacity and GPU fleet consistency.
- Product (Nikhil Sharma / Henry Cho): aligns thresholds with customer expectations and release risk policy.

High-level timeline/phases (typical ~6–10 weeks):
1) Definition & design (week 1–2): choose canary models/SKUs, metrics, noise model, threshold policy; write spec + ADRs.
2) Implementation (week 2–6): perf-canary runner, CI jobs, baseline store, report artifacts, dashboards.
3) Rollout (week 6–8): shadow mode (report-only), calibrate thresholds, then enable blocking for runtime release branches.
4) Hardening (week 8–10): flake reduction, capacity protections, incident/runbook updates, and ongoing governance.

Key deliverables:
- A perf canary service/job that runs deterministically in CI and on scheduled cadence.
- A threshold/baseline policy (per metric, per model, per GPU) with guardrails for variance.
- CI integration that fails checks and blocks release promotion when thresholds are exceeded.
- Dashboards and triage runbooks (who investigates, how to bisect, how to override with approvals).

Constraints/risks:
- Benchmark noise (thermal, neighbor contention, driver differences) can cause false positives; mitigation includes pinned images/drivers, dedicated canary nodes, warmup, repeated runs, and robust statistics.
- Cost/capacity: GPU time is expensive; keep canary suite short and prioritized, with a longer nightly suite.
- Governance: need an override/exception process for justified regressions (e.g., memory safety fix) with explicit approvals and customer impact sign-off.

files.description: High-level overview of the CI perf regression gate: why it exists, what it blocks, which repos/pipelines are covered, and ownership/SLAs for responding to failures.
Definition of canary workloads (prompt sets, sequence length distributions, prefill/decode mix), required metrics (TTFT, tokens/sec, p95 latency, memory), and how runs are standardized.
Policy doc specifying thresholds per metric/model/GPU, noise handling rules (minimum samples, confidence), and what constitutes a release-block vs. warn-only.
ADR capturing the decision for baseline source (last-good release vs rolling), storage location, comparison algorithm, and rationale/trade-offs.
ADR describing how CI signals map to release gating (required checks, branch protections, release train promotion rules) and override procedure.
Dashboard requirements for perf canary trends: per GPU/model charts, regression annotations, links to CI runs/PRs, and alert thresholds.
Step-by-step runbook for responding to a gate failure: verify flake vs real regression, rerun protocol, bisect guidance, escalation path, and communications.
Defines when perf regressions become incidents, severity mapping, paging rules, and customer communication triggers.
Initiative ticket: “CI Performance Regression Gate (Hosted models + top GPUs)” with goals, scope, milestones (shadow mode → blocking), and cross-team owners.
Epic: Build perf-canary runner (repo perf-canary) with workload definition, execution harness, artifact upload, and retries.
Task: Define baseline storage format and retention (e.g., S3/GCS + metadata) and implement baseline fetch/compare library.
Task: CI integration in redwood repo (GitHub Actions or internal CI) including required checks, PR annotations, and release branch protections.
Task: Observability pipeline for canary results (metrics ingestion + labels for model/GPU/driver/runtime version).
Task: Calibrate thresholds using 2 weeks of shadow data; propose final block/warn settings and sign-off checklist.
PM ticket: customer-facing implications of perf gates (release velocity vs reliability), and definition of acceptable regressions for top hosted models.
PR adding initial perf-canary CLI runner: config schema for model/GPU matrix, warmup protocol, and JSON result output.
PR implementing baseline comparison and threshold evaluation (including variance handling) producing pass/fail and a human-readable report.
PR wiring runtime build artifacts into the canary job (pin runtime commit, container image tags, driver/toolkit version capture).
PR adding CI required check “perf-gate (canary)” for release branches; includes rerun instructions and override labeling mechanism.
PR adding dashboards/metrics definitions for canary results and regression alerts; includes tag conventions (gpu_sku, model_id, runtime_version).
Thread coordinating rollout plan for shadow mode and when to flip blocking on; includes concerns about release velocity and override policy.
Thread debugging a suspected regression caught by canary; runtime engineers compare kernels/scheduler changes and discuss bisect strategy.
Thread on canary capacity and GPU node pinning; infra discusses dedicated canary pool, driver pinning, and neighbor-noise mitigation.
Thread reviewing alerting strategy for canary regressions and how it ties into oncall/incident process.
Working checklist for rollout: shadow mode steps, threshold calibration plan, stakeholders sign-off, and backout/disable procedure.
Spreadsheet-style doc (table) summarizing shadow runs across models/GPUs with observed variance and proposed thresholds.
Draft dashboard layout and queries, including example panels for TTFT p95, tokens/sec, memory headroom, and regression annotations.
Support ticket: customer reports latency spike after a runtime update; investigation notes reference canary results and a blocked release/hotfix.
Internal ticket: CI perf gate flaky failures; root cause analysis (capacity contention / warmup) and remediation tasks.
Email thread among Release Eng + SRE leadership: proposal to enforce perf gate as required check for runtime release branches; includes risk/mitigation and timeline.
Leadership escalation email: canary caught regression hours before planned release; decision to delay, comms plan, and follow-ups.
Technical deep dive transcript with an enterprise prospect asking about performance guarantees; Redwood explains regression gates, canaries, and SLO monitoring.
CRM company record for an enterprise account evaluating Dedicated; notes include performance sensitivity, questions about release controls, and linked technical deep dive.
